distribution_family.justification: Public analytics provides clear empirical limits on two-point conversion rates, leading to a symmetric distribution around the expected win-probability gain.
distribution_family.name: normal

parameters.conversion_note: Calculated for normal distribution: mu = 0.35; sigma = (interval_95_high - interval_95_low) / 3.92 = (0.65 - 0.05) / 3.92 ≈ 0.153.

strategies.rationale: Published win-probability models demonstrate that attempting the two-point conversion on the first touchdown maximizes regulation win probability compared to kicking two extra points, which defaults the game to an equal-odds overtime.
strategies.recommendation: Attempt a two-point conversion immediately after scoring a touchdown when trailing by 14 points in the fourth quarter. If successful, the team trails by 6 points and can win on the next touchdown with a point-after kick; if unsuccessful, a second two-point attempt can still tie the game.
strategies.title: Down-14 Two-Point Conversion Protocol

strategies.rationale: Expected Points Added (EPA) models consistently show that early-down passing generates higher EPA per play than early-down rushing, significantly reducing the frequency of third-and-long situations.
strategies.recommendation: Increase 1st & 10 pass rate to at least 65% in neutral game states (win probability between 20% and 80%) across the first three quarters. Focus on short-to-intermediate high-completion concepts and play-action sequences to consistently move into second-and-manageable.
strategies.title: Neutral-State Early-Down Passing Bias

strategies.rationale: Analytics models establish that preventing passing explosives yields far higher expected points saved than defending against incremental rushing gains, making light-box run concessions mathematically favorable.
strategies.recommendation: Maintain a two-high safety shell (Cover 4 / Cover 6) on early downs even when the opponent deploys heavy personnel groupings (12 or 22 personnel). Accept a light box against the run to prioritize eliminating explosive passing plays over the top.
strategies.title: Two-High Safety Shell Against Heavy Personnel

strategies.rationale: Public analytics models treat quarter breaks as neutral administrative resets and do not model fatigue accumulation across quarter transitions. Coaching intuition indicates that forcing exhausted defensive personnel to stay on the field across quarter breaks creates mental miscommunications and physical mismatches.
strategies.recommendation: Shift to a rapid no-huddle pace with under 90 seconds remaining in the 1st and 3rd quarters while keeping the same offensive personnel. Lock tired or schematically unfavorable defensive personnel on the field across the quarter transition.
strategies.title: End-of-Quarter Tempo Acceleration to Trap Personnel

strategies.rationale: Public analytics tracks personnel efficiency and formation width independently, remaining silent on the interaction effect of spreading heavy packages. Coaching intuition indicates that defensive personnel calls match offensive personnel, giving athletic tight ends clear spatial advantages against linebackers.
strategies.recommendation: Deploy 13 personnel (1 RB, 3 TE, 1 WR) on 1st down but split all three tight ends wide in a 5-wide empty alignment. Force opposing linebackers and safeties into open-field coverage responsibilities against athletic tight ends.
strategies.title: Positionless Heavy-Personnel Spread Formations

strategies.rationale: Public analytics evaluates pre-snap alignment at snap time but lacks data on cognitive overload caused by late shifts under tight play-clock constraints. Coaching experience shows that late movement induces panicked offensive protection resets, resulting in false starts and unblocked rushers.
strategies.recommendation: Order front-seven defenders to hold static pre-snap positions until under 4 seconds remain on the play clock, then rapidly stem into new gap alignments or creeping blitz tracks.
strategies.title: Late Play-Clock Defensive Line Stemming
